solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Peer defending company against international revolutionary? It’s unclear

indicators.note: to defend something is to stand around it, so one piece encloses the others
a revolution is a turning round, so the letters it governs are run backwards

blocks.note: a peer is an equal
CO is the abbreviation for company
V for versus, against
I is the abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: A lord takes the side of a company facing a rebel from abroad, and the whole affair is murky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a nobleman but means an equal. 'Against' is V for versus, a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something equivocal is ambiguous, open to more than one interpretation, so its meaning is not clear.

clue.text: Survey discovered English succeed

indicators.note: dis-covered means with its cover taken off, so the outer letters go

blocks.note: a census is an official survey of the population
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A study finds that English people do well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' is read as dis-covered: CENSUS loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed in the sense of coming after, follow on, is what one event does when it results from another.

clue.text: Service providers united with instiitute acquired by elitist rogue

indicators.note: what is acquired is taken in and held, so one letter goes inside the other word
a rogue goes off the rails and behaves unpredictably, so the letters break out of their order

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for united, as in football club names
taken as written
the first letter of institute, misprinted in the clue, used as its abbreviation

explanation.surface: Utility firms join forces with a research institute that has been bought up by a snobbish maverick.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes into ELITIST and the eight letters are rearranged after U.
explanation.definitionFit: Utilities are the companies that supply gas, electricity and water to homes and businesses.

clue.text: Endangered, blue raven flying across lake

indicators.note: things flying are scattered through the air, so the letters land in a new order
lying across something means spanning it, so the letters straddle the single one

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A rare blue raven, a protected species, flies over a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of BLUE RAVEN is arranged around L for lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Vulnerable is the conservation category for species facing a high risk of extinction, close kin to endangered.

clue.text: Routine task interrupted by extremely theatrical laugh

indicators.note: an interruption breaks into the middle of something, so letters are inserted
the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outer letters count

blocks.note: a chore is a routine household job
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A dull job gets interrupted by somebody's loud, stagey laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely theatrical' sounds like a description of the laugh, but it only supplies two edge letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A chortle is a gleeful chuckle, a word coined by Lewis Carroll blending chuckle and snort.

clue.text: City on river the Spanish festooned with American shrubs

indicators.note: festoons are garlands draped around something, so one piece is wrapped in another

blocks.note: LA is Los Angeles
US for American
R is the abbreviation for river
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A riverside city, Spanish in character, is decked out with American bushes.
explanation.walkthrough: LA comes first; then R+EL is garlanded by US to give U-REL-S.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurels are evergreen shrubs such as bay and cherry laurel, often grown as hedging.

clue.text: Fail to include line in entertaining book’s conclusion

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so a letter is placed within
the word says where the letter goes: inside the following pieces
a conclusion is the end, so only the final letter of the word is used

blocks.note: something entertaining is fun
L is the abbreviation for line
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone forgets to quote a line in the end of an amusing novel.
explanation.walkthrough: FUN plus K, the end of 'book', takes in L after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Flunk is informal, mainly American, for failing an exam or course.

clue.text: Tricks disheartened adversaries

indicators.note: losing heart means losing the middle, so the central letter is removed

blocks.note: to fox is to trick or baffle

explanation.surface: Clever tricks leave opponents dispirited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tricks' is a verb here: FOXES, which loses its central X.
explanation.definitionFit: Foes are enemies or opponents, the people one is set against.

clue.text: Free group of soldiers one sent south-east

indicators.note: something sent is moved from where it was, so it leaves its place and travels down

blocks.note: a unit is a body of troops
Roman numeral one
east, the last point of the compass bearing

explanation.surface: A squad is released with one of its men posted to the south-east.
explanation.walkthrough: In UNIT the I is sent south, down to the bottom of this down entry, and E for east follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie is to undo knots or bonds, setting something or someone loose.

clue.text: Cold-blooded type runs over detective tracking crucial computer components

indicators.note: tracking means following behind, so the earlier pieces come after the next one

blocks.note: key means crucial
a boa is a snake, a cold-blooded reptile
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
DS is a Detective Sergeant

explanation.surface: A heartless villain runs over a detective who has been tracking vital computer parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold-blooded type' suggests a ruthless criminal but is literally a reptile. 'Over' simply places one piece above the next in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard is the input device of a computer, the set of keys used for typing.

clue.text: Even now, some call it sleeping around

indicators.note: some means a portion, so the letters are a run lifted from inside the phrase
turned around means facing the other way, so the run reads backwards

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the first word, the second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Some would say that even now a certain person is sleeping around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleeping around' tempts as a phrase, but 'around' acts alone on the letters spanning 'caLL IT Sleeping'.
explanation.definitionFit: Still as an adverb means up to this time, as in 'still waiting'.

clue.text: Dressed up on telly in lavish fashion

indicators.note: dressing is preparing or arranging, so the letters are set out anew

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A TV presenter appears dressed up extravagantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressed up' reads as one phrase, but only 'Dressed' signals; 'up' belongs in the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something opulently is to do it with ostentatious richness and luxury.

clue.text: Focal points of poems claiming watchman unmasked earl

indicators.note: to claim is to take possession, so the outer word holds the others
with the mask removed, the outer covering is stripped off, losing first and last letters

blocks.note: epics are long narrative poems
a sentry is a guard on watch
E is the abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: Key passages in poems describe a watchman exposing an earl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unmasked earl' tempts as one phrase, but 'unmasked' acts on the watchman and the earl is just E.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicentre is literally the ground point above an earthquake, figuratively the heart or focus of activity.

clue.text: A duck hiding in prize rosebush

indicators.note: something hiding in a place is concealed within it, so the letters lie inside the words

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A duck is lurking in a prize-winning rose bush.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird is a cricket duck: a batsman's score of nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a duck is a score of nought, named from the egg-like shape of 0.

clue.text: Protest threw light on satellite nation’s ultimate destruction

indicators.note: ultimate means final, so only the last letter of the word is used

blocks.note: a demo is a demonstration
lit is the past tense of light, to illuminate
Io is a moon of Jupiter
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A protest exposed a client state's final ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Satellite nation' looks like a political phrase; split it, 'satellite' is the moon IO and 'nation's ultimate' is N.
explanation.definitionFit: Demolition is the knocking down of a building, and more widely any complete destruction.

clue.text: Expert put on edge by German’s pained expression

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for German
a rim is an edge
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A specialist, made nervous by a German, pulls a face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on edge' looks like 'made nervous', but here it just orders the pieces: the expert follows the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimace is a twisted facial look showing pain, disgust or distaste.

clue.text: General rule Steerpike breaks in deluge at sea

indicators.note: breaking in means forcing an entry, so one letter goes inside the others
at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: Steerpike is the setter, who refers to himself as I
taken as written

explanation.surface: The setter flouts a broad principle while caught in a storm on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter naming himself in the clue means I. That I breaks into 'in deluge' and all nine letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A guideline is a general principle or piece of advice that guides conduct, not a strict law.

clue.text: Train spy

blocks.note: first meaning: an overnight train with beds
second meaning: an agent planted to lie dormant until activated

explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a verb, to train a spy, but both words are nouns naming separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeper is both a night train with berths and a secret agent who lives undercover for years before acting.

clue.text: Influence cost, keeping Japan in trading alliance with Germany

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold on to it, so the outer word holds the rest
the word says where the letter sits: inside the next piece

blocks.note: a price is a cost
the European Union, a trading bloc
J is the international vehicle code for Japan
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: Economic sway costs something, keeping Japan inside a trade bloc with Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: J and D are international vehicle registration codes, a common crossword source for single letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To prejudice is to sway or bias someone's judgement in advance, a verb sense of influence.

clue.text: Hollow toolmarks on giant skull oddly dismissed as wounds

indicators.note: a hollow thing keeps its shell and loses its inside, so only the outer letters remain
sending away the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even ones
in an across entry, sitting on something means coming after it, so the first-named piece goes second

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Hollow tool marks on the skull of a giant are dismissed as mere injuries.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' puts TS after the letters from 'giant skull'. 'Wounds' is a verb, not the injuries of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulting someone hurts their feelings, so an insult wounds in the emotional sense.

clue.text: Gave rise to endless Native Americans entering South Dakota

indicators.note: with no end, the final letter is cut off
to enter is to go inside, so these letters are placed within the others

blocks.note: SD is the postal abbreviation for South Dakota
the Pawnee are a Native American people of the Great Plains

explanation.surface: Native Americans moving into South Dakota gave rise to something.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as history of the Plains; the Pawnee did live near the Dakotas, which helps the picture hold together.
explanation.definitionFit: To spawn is to produce or generate, as fish lay eggs, so spawned means caused to come into being.

clue.text: Summits see Republicans beginning to attract backing

indicators.note: a beginning is the start, so only the first letter of the word counts
going backwards means the whole string is written from right to left

blocks.note: taken as written
the GOP, Grand Old Party, is the US Republican Party
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: At summit meetings Republicans start to win support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summits' suggests political meetings; it is the definition, and 'backing' reverses everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: An apogee is the highest point of an orbit and so, figuratively, a peak or climax.

clue.text: Idiot crushed by article in port

indicators.note: being crushed means lying beneath, so in a down entry this piece sits below

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article
a twerp is a silly person

explanation.surface: A fool is flattened by a news story down at the docks.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, being crushed by something means lying under it, so AN goes on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Antwerp in Belgium is one of Europe's largest seaports.

clue.text: Test drug before ten in the morning

blocks.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
Roman numeral ten
am, ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: A drug test is scheduled for before ten in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ten in the morning' reads as a time but splits into X and AM.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a formal test of knowledge or skill.

clue.text: Grant is a flipping lottery!

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the letters are put the other way

blocks.note: taken as written
a draw is a lottery or raffle

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that the allocation of funds is a damned lottery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' poses as a mild British curse word but turns DRAW round.
explanation.definitionFit: A grant is a sum of money awarded, and an award is a payment or prize given.

clue.text: Cured ailments consuming upper-class model at the eleventh hour

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; the definition is an adverbial phrase

indicators.note: a cured complaint has been treated and set right, so the letters are reworked
to consume is to take inside, so the outer letters swallow the others

blocks.note: taken as written
U means upper class in British usage
the Model T Ford

explanation.surface: A posh model's illnesses were cured at the very last moment.
explanation.walkthrough: AILMENTS takes in U and T, and all ten letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Last-minute describes something done just before a deadline, when time has almost run out.

clue.text: Boat crew scoffed audibly

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the sound of the word is what matters

blocks.note: to scoff is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: The rowing team noisily wolfed down their meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffed' could mean mocked, but here it is the British slang sense of eating greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing eight is a racing boat with eight oarsmen, and by extension the crew rowing it.

clue.text: Declare absolute victory over Welsh

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for absolute, as in temperature scales
V for victory
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
W is the abbreviation for Welsh

explanation.surface: Someone proclaims a total win over Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word is a single-letter abbreviation; 'over' is the cricket O, not a positional word.
explanation.definitionFit: To avow is to state openly or affirm, a formal synonym of declare.

clue.text: Upfront attorney turned on popular vice-president

indicators.note: turned means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: in means popular, fashionable
a DA is an American district attorney
JD Vance, US vice-president

explanation.surface: A frank lawyer rounded on a well-liked vice-president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upfront' seems to describe the attorney as candid, but it is the definition in its paying-beforehand sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Payment upfront is payment made beforehand, before goods or services are delivered.

clue.text: Islands around Cuba leaders in naturally grown sugar product

indicators.note: being around something means enclosing it, so these letters surround the next
leaders go in front, so only the first letter of each word is taken

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for island, doubled for the plural
C is the international vehicle code for Cuba
the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Caribbean islands near Cuba lead the way in organic sugar products.
explanation.walkthrough: II wraps around C, and the first letters of 'naturally grown' follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing is a sweet coating for cakes made chiefly from icing sugar.

clue.text: Give money to discontented European women after party

indicators.note: with the contents emptied out, only the outer shell of the word survives
coming after means following behind, so this letter is placed later

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
a do is a party
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: Unhappy European women are handed cash after a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discontented' passes for unhappy but means emptied out. A do is British slang for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to provide a permanent income or fund, as for a college or prize.

clue.text: Journalist catches writer in study essentially importuning subordinate

indicators.note: to catch is to take hold, so the outer letters enclose the inner one
the word says where the combined letters go: inside the following piece
the essence of a word is its very core, so only the middle letter is taken

blocks.note: a den is a private study
an ed is an editor
a pen is a writing instrument
the central letter of the eleven

explanation.surface: A reporter catches an author in the study, basically pestering a junior colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest here, one inside the other, before the middle letter of 'importuning' closes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dependent means reliant on or subject to another, so it describes something in an inferior position.
